title: Bean lifecycle
context: What are the steps in the lifecycle of a Spring bean?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: The container instantiates the bean, populates its properties with dependencies, and calls the Aware callbacks such as BeanNameAware and ApplicationContextAware. Each BeanPostProcessor's before method runs. Then init runs: @PostConstruct, then InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet, then a custom init-method. The after method of each BeanPostProcessor runs, and the bean is ready. On shutdown, @PreDestroy, DisposableBean.destroy and a custom destroy method run. Proxies such as AOP wrappers are usually created by a post-processor.

points.title: Order of init
points.why: @PostConstruct runs before afterPropertiesSet, which runs before a custom init-method.

points.title: Post-processors
points.why: BeanPostProcessors run around init and can replace the bean with a proxy.

points.title: Destruction
points.why: @PreDestroy and destroy run only for singletons on context close.
